raw.title: feat(runner): support cross-document workflowId references
raw.body:
Closes #64.

A workflow reference written as `$sourceDescriptions.<name>.<workflowId>` now resolves and runs in all four author-facing positions — a sub-workflow step's `workflowId`, a `dependsOn` entry, a `retry` action's `workflowId` reference, and a `goto`'s transfer target. `WorkflowExecutor.#rejectCrossDocumentWorkflow` and `reason: 'cross-document-workflow-unsupported'` are gone.

## Design

- **Canonical form is a locator, not a string.** Every reference — plain id or expression — normalizes through a new public `ArazzoWorkflowLocatorNormalizer` to `ArazzoWorkflowLocator {document, workflowId}`, mirroring `OpenAPIOperationLocator` (registry in the constructor, referencing document per call). A canonical *string* form was considered and rejected: the entry document's own workflows have no expression spelling, and source names are document-scoped, so the expression form is not context-free. Sync `parseReference` serves state keys and the retry-pinned `$workflows` entry without awaiting; only the dotted spec form is accepted — the resolver's `#/workflows/...` pointer form is a `$ref`-time construct, not a runtime expression.
- **The document moved into the invocation.** `WorkflowInvocation.document`, `#run(locator, …)`, `#resolveWorkflow(locator, scope)`, and the `#evaluate` bridge take the invocation's document, so a foreign workflow's id lookups, its steps' operations, and its `$components`/`$sourceDescriptions` expressions all resolve against the document that owns it. Parent-side evaluation of a sub-workflow step (parameters, outputs, criteria, action selection) stays on the *parent's* document — only the sub-run switches.
- **`StepExecutor` stays document-bound** — the seam from #34 is untouched (no per-call document argument, no factory option). A new `forDocument(document)` derives a sibling bound to a foreign document, sharing the registry and operation executor; `WorkflowExecutor` caches one per document URI per run, seeded with the injected instance.
- **Identity is `{documentURI}#{workflowId}`** for cycle detection, the normalized-workflow cache, and `dependsOn` memoization — passed always, entry document included, so a foreign source pointing back at the entry closes a detectable cycle and two documents' workflows sharing an id do not falsely form one. Error `path` displays bare ids for entry-document frames (keeping every existing path assertion) and `uri#id` for foreign ones.
- **`$workflows.<id>` state stays keyed by the bare id** — the only form the runtime-expression grammar can express; the cross-document collision hazard (last-write-wins, same class as two same-document calls of one workflow) is documented in the README and flagged in the plan doc.
- **`dependencyInputs` is keyed by the `dependsOn` entry as written** — bare id locally, the whole expression cross-document.
- **A per-run document ledger** (`RunScope.documents`) keeps every in-use document alive against the registry's size-4 LRU; the pre-existing sync `registry.get` expression-time exposure is recorded as a known limitation in the plan doc.

## Errors

`ExecutionError` with `invalid-workflow-reference` (a `$`-prefixed reference that is not a `$sourceDescriptions` expression), `source-description-not-found`, `source-description-not-arazzo` (sources classified by what they parse to via `ArazzoDocument.is`, never the declared `type:`), or `workflow-not-found` naming the document actually searched.

## Tests

- New `WorkflowExecutorCrossDocument` suite (15 tests) over a two-document fixture pair whose APIs have distinct server prefixes, so a recorded request URL proves which document's source descriptions resolved an operation — the silently-wrong hazard is asserted directly. Covers all four positions, foreign-document expression bases, a foreign workflow's own local references resolving in its own document, same-id-no-false-cycle, a genuine cross-document cycle with mixed-display `path`, depth across documents, `dependencyInputs` literal-key delivery, diamond memoization, whole-list `dependsOn` validation before any request, abort-before-resolution at the transfer boundary, and every new error reason.
- 3 new `WorkflowCallStack` qualified-key unit tests; existing bare-id tests unchanged.
- The four old rejection tests are repurposed, not dropped: their fixtures reference a workflow of an *openapi* source, so they now assert `source-description-not-arazzo`, keeping the validate-before-run (`calls.length === 0`) and abort-ordering assertions.

## Docs

README: new "Cross-document workflow references" section; "Not yet supported" removed; `StepExecutor` description tightened (it runs operation-shaped steps — `workflowId` steps are run by `WorkflowExecutor`, which borrows its criteria/action evaluation). `WORKFLOW_EXECUTOR_PLAN.md`: the analysis moved into a §0 "Shipped (cross-document workflow references)" entry recording each decision; loose ends updated (duplicated `#evaluate` bridges, expression-time eviction exposure, `$workflows` id-collision).

`npm run test` (546 passing), `npm run lint`, and `tsc --noEmit` are clean.
